This patch changes a few things.  Hopefully the comments are helpfull
I'll try and be as verbose here.
Problem:
My fedora box was taking 1 minute and 21 seconds to boot with btrfs as root.
Part of this problem was we pick the first block group we can find and start
caching it
column2: even if it may not have enough free space.  The other problem is

column1: we only search for cached block groups the first time around
find any cached block groups because this is a newly mounted fs
caching several block groups during bootup
takes around 30-45 seconds to complete
column2: which bogs down the system.  So

column1: Solution:
1) Don't cache block groups willy-nilly at first.  Instead try and figure out
which block group has the most free
column2: and therefore will take the least amount

column1: of time to cache.
2) Don't be so picky about cached block groups.  The other problem is once
we've filled up a cluster
column2: if the block group isn't finished caching the next

column1: time we try and do the allocation we'll completely ignore the cluster and
start searching from the beginning of the space
block groups
column2: which slows us down even more.  So instead of skipping block

column1: groups that are not finished caching when we have a hint
group if it hasn't started caching yet.
There is one other tweak in here.  Before if we allocated a chunk and still
couldn't find new space
column2: we'd end up switching the space info to force another

column1: chunk allocation.  This could make us end up with way too many chunks
track of this particular case.
With this patch and my previous cluster fixes my fedora box now boots in 43
seconds
column2: and according to the bootchart is not held up by our block group

column1: caching at all.
